I ran a paired t-test on the new-book prices from the UCLA bookstore and Amazon. It used the 68 textbooks that have both prices. The test pairs each book's two prices, so the standard error comes from the per-book price differences.

- Mean difference (bookstore minus Amazon): about $3.58
- Standard error of the difference: about 1.63
- t = 2.20 with 67 degrees of freedom, p ≈ 0.031

At the 5% level, this rejects the null hypothesis of no difference. New books cost more at the bookstore than on Amazon on average.

ANSWER: 1.63
